title: Automatic listening location changes are mistaken for manual chapter navigation
symptom: Following playback into another chapter or opening a paused notification's chapter can change the session to STOPPED_BY_NAVIGATION.
root_cause: StablePageReaderContent emitted the same stop-on-cross-chapter callback for every confirmed chapter change, without distinguishing accepted user page turns from semantic anchor jumps initiated by listening.
fix: Inspect the still-pending navigation request before confirmation clears it. Emit manual cross-chapter navigation only when that request contains accepted page-turn input.
Listening follow, notification opening and explicit continuation use anchor jumps without that manual input. Directory and explicit chapter buttons retain their existing stop behavior.
evidence: pausedNotificationOpensListeningTextWhileOrdinaryOpeningKeepsReadingPosition reproduced PAUSED_BY_USER becoming STOPPED_BY_NAVIGATION after locating the correct chapter, and passes after correction.

pageModeFollowsPlaybackIntoSpokenChapter now checks that PLAYING survives automatic chapter follow and passes. pageBoundaryTurnStopsActiveTtsBeforeOpeningAdjacentChapter also passes, preserving actual user-navigation semantics.
impact: The covered complete-reader paths now preserve the intended distinction between following listening and deliberately navigating away. The regression uses controlled playback snapshots; actual audio and screen-off behavior have separate evidence.
